findings.net: YIWU TENGDING's VenKuri would probably lose against the company’s VENQORI water-quality software and training in Japan, although a registration objection remains possible.
findings.legal_position: VenKuri's BENKURI reading is close to VENQORI, but the earlier owner is likely to lose on the stated software-and-training use: its registered goods are cameras and non-medical surveillance apparatus (among broad goods), not downloadable software or training. The Japanese measuring/testing classification leaves a possible registration objection, while the O/U sound difference in the middle syllable and narrower goods provide good defences.
findings.practical_position: Actual products, Japanese sales channels and enforcement appetite are unverified, so no dormancy, non-use or low-enforcement mitigation is applied. The live Japanese registration supports residual challenge risk, but neither competing water-quality software nor a need for consent is established.

byOrdinal.body:
**Question grounded:** How should the close recorded pronunciation be weighed when assessing a possible Japanese registration objection?

**On-point authority:**
- *商標登録願拒絶査定抗告審判審決取消請求* (SINGER / SHINKA) · Supreme Court of Japan, Third Petty Bench · 4 October 1960 · holding: the court upheld a finding that the pronunciations were similar in the concrete trading circumstances, including the fame of SINGER sewing machines, even though an abstract comparison might not establish similarity · [judgment](https://www.courts.go.jp/hanrei/52938/detail2/index.html).
  — relevance: pronunciation must be considered in the actual trading context. The decision involved a famous sewing-machine mark and an older statutory provision; it does not decide whether VENQORI and VenKuri are similar or whether the respective goods and services are related.

**Coverage gaps:** Legal Data Hunter's Japanese court collection was searched for the owner, VenKuri and trademark similarity. The returned owner and mark searches did not identify an on-point enforcement proceeding. This does not establish the owner's enforcement history or its absence. Japanese Patent Office opposition and appeal decisions were not searched; the court search is not exhaustive. No commercial citator was consulted.

Those goods are not treated as unrelated merely because the specification emphasizes autonomous driving. The complete two-word mark WOVEN CORE has the separate WOVEN onset, CORE ending and recorded UOOBUNKOA/UUBUNKOA reading, materially different from the coined unit VENQORI and its searched VENKORI/VENCORI forms. No active same-field consumer water-app brand or famous-neighbour evidence overrides that comparison. The cancelled Woven CORE application of the same owner is considered alongside this live right.

ProvenCore is a live international registration expressly designating JP; it is not discarded as a foreign-only right. Its class-9 wording includes computer programs (downloadable software), and its class-42 wording includes software design and maintenance, so registered scope can meet the client's software despite the security/IoT emphasis. Comparing whole marks, PROVENCORE retains the conspicuous PRO onset and the separate recognizable PROVEN/CORE construction and CORE ending, unlike VENQORI or VENKORI. Shared internal ven/cor letters do not establish a plausible conflict here. Current use as a consumer water-monitoring brand and famous-neighbour status are not shown. The ground is the whole-mark comparison, not a missing water-related goods word or an assumption about Japanese designation status.

sections.Marks:
## YIWU TENGDING UMBRELLA CO., LTD. — ＶＥＮＫＵＲＩ
- ord: 1
- open: true
- net: YIWU TENGDING's VenKuri would probably lose against the company’s VENQORI water-quality software and training in Japan, although a registration objection remains possible.
- group: on-field
- source: Register
### Full detail

- **Risk assessment.** YIWU TENGDING's Ｖｅｎｋｕｒｉ has the recorded reading BENKURI, close to VENQORI. Its registered goods include cameras and non-medical surveillance apparatus, not downloadable software or training. The O/U sound difference and narrower goods provide good defences, although the Japanese measuring and testing classification leaves a possible registration objection.
- **Authority.** In [SINGER / SHINKA](https://www.courts.go.jp/hanrei/52938/detail2/index.html), Japan's Supreme Court considered pronunciation in the actual trading circumstances. That decision involved a famous sewing-machine mark and does not decide similarity or the relationship between these goods and services.
- **Use.** Actual products and Japanese sales channels are unverified; competing water-quality software is not established.
- **Enforcement.** The owner's enforcement appetite is unverified. The Japanese court search did not identify an on-point proceeding, but does not establish the owner's enforcement history.
sections.Reasoned negatives: None. Every retrieved close match on this run is an on-field conflict above — nothing was cleared into this section.
